title: Machine-Checked Exact-Rational Tower Transition, d-Closed Barrier, and Outward-Witness Certificates for Majority Bootstrap Percolation
abstract: Vyacheslav Koval and Yuval Peres (arXiv:2611.33087, November 24, 2026) resolved the high-dimensional phase transition of majority (d-neighbour) bootstrap percolation on the discrete torus Z_n^d, proving a sharp tower transition (Theorem 1.1): when H(n)/d -> rho in [0,1] (with H(n) = log*_2 n), the critical density converges to p_rho = (1-rho)/(2-rho), recovering Morris's p = 1/4 <-> rho = 2/3 threshold (Corollary 1.2) and contrasting sharply with the dyadic box limit p_c([n]^d) -> 1 - 2^{-m} at n/d = 1/m (Eq. 1.2). We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formalization and exact-Q certificate auditor for the algebraic, combinatorial, barrier-closure, and finite-scale geometric core of these results. An 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (BootstrapTowerTransition.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice, 3 zero-axiom theorems) formalizes the tetration tower T_0..T_4, strict monotonicity, the exact cleared bijection p_rho <-> rho_p, Morris's (2/3,1/4) point, expected-support balance v+(2d-v)p=d, inductive Eq. (2.3) d-closed layer closure over arbitrary lists, abstract monotone closure, Lemma 2.1 geodesic overlap margins, Eq. (1.2) dyadic box gaps 1-2^{-m} > 1/2, and Lemma 2.3 rectangle-merge hull bounds. BOOTSTRAP-TOWER-CERT-1.0 audits four exact-Q modes—tower-curve bijections, exact finite Z_n^d/[n]^d filling and Eq. (2.3) d-closed barriers, exact rational Lemma 2.1 binomial tails w_0, and dyadic box limits with l_inf > 2t separated rectangles—replaying 16 canonical certificates in 0.036-0.446 ms and rejecting 60/60 live adversarial forgeries.
